items.context: eventlog_setup.go currently builds a custom DSN with WAL pragmas (journal_mode=WAL, busy_timeout=10000, synchronous=NORMAL) and passes it to sql.Open. database.Connect supports explicit DSN passthrough but also has its own buildSQLiteDSN that reads SQLITE_PATH from env. The current code uses a storage.Resolver to find the DB path, not env vars. We need to decide whether to keep the custom DSN logic or adapt to the env-based approach.

options.label: Pass existing DSN directly to database.Connect
options.rationale: Keep resolveEventDBPath() as-is. Pass its output as Config.DSN to database.Connect. This is the lowest-risk change — preserves all existing path resolution and pragma logic while satisfying the standards requirement to use the shared connection helper. Recommended because it minimizes behavioral changes while fixing the violation.

options.label: Refactor to use SQLITE_PATH env var
options.rationale: Set SWARM_MANAGER_SQLITE_PATH in the lifecycle system and let database.Connect read it via buildSQLiteDSN. Cleaner long-term but requires lifecycle config changes and loses the storage.Resolver fallback chain and WAL pragmas.

items.notes: Pre-selected because Option A is clearly the lowest-risk path that satisfies the standard.

items.topic: Test depth for dispatch and logging packages
items.context: dispatch/ defines two interfaces (Invalidator, NodeDispatcher) with no concrete implementation — the graph package implements them. logging/ has 4 small functions (Init, WithLogger, FromContext, With). Standards require test files exist, but test depth matters for maintainability.

options.label: Minimal compile-check tests for dispatch; functional tests for logging
options.rationale: dispatch/ only has interfaces — test that a mock type satisfies them (compile-time guarantee). logging/ has real behavior worth testing: context round-trip, Init() configures slog, With() returns child logger. Recommended because it matches the actual testable surface of each package.

options.label: Minimal placeholder tests for both
options.rationale: Just enough to make standards pass (e.g., TestPackageImports). Fast to write but adds no real value.

items.context: cli/go.mod uses Go 1.22 while api/go.mod uses Go 1.24. The standards flag says 'Go CLI builds without workspace mode'. No go.work file exists anywhere in the swarm-manager scenario. The CLI module has replace directives pointing to ../api and packages/cli-core.

options.label: Create go.work at scenarios/swarm-manager/ with api and cli modules
options.rationale: A go.work file at the scenario root listing both ./api and ./cli modules enables workspace mode. This is the standard Go approach for multi-module repos and eliminates the need for replace directives in cli/go.mod. Recommended because it directly addresses the 'without workspace mode' violation.

options.label: Just upgrade cli/go.mod to Go 1.24 and keep replace directives
options.rationale: Fixes the Go version mismatch but may not fully resolve the 'workspace mode' warning if the standard specifically requires go.work.

items.text: database.Connect in api-core fully supports SQLite: DriverSQLite constant exists (line 53), buildSQLiteDSN reads SQLITE_PATH/SQLITE_DB, and Config.DSN allows explicit passthrough. The migration to database.Connect is straightforward — the current resolveEventDBPath() output can be passed as Config.DSN directly.

cli/cmd/migrate_workshop.go (626 lines) has rich testable surface: clarifyToRound, suggestToRound, computeReadiness, mapSuggestionStatus, answerString, and file helpers. These are all package-level functions that can be tested with table-driven tests using in-memory fixtures (no file I/O mocking needed for the conversion helpers).
